program.ffr_notes: The two other local files (FR Doc. 2025-13972, 2025-07-24, the MOSAIC light-sport special airworthiness final rule; FR Doc. 2026-14298, 2026-07-16, the ASTM light-sport consensus standards NOA) do not mention eIPP. They are related regulatory context, not eIPP notices, so they are left out of ffr_notices.
program.summary: DOT and FAA set up the eIPP under the Unleashing Drone Dominance Executive Order. It pairs state, local, tribal and territorial governments with US AAM companies to fly pre-certification operations that generate data for future FAA rules. More than 30 proposals came in, and eight were selected on 2026-03-09. The program runs for three years after the first project becomes operational. Each project starts under an Other Transaction Agreement, which begins a 90-day clock to start operations. No OTA had been signed as of 2026-06-09. The first operational flight was BETA's organ-transport mission for the PennDOT-led collaborative on 2026-07-10. By 2026-10-19 the FAA counted six launched locations (PA collaborative, UT, LA, TX, NC, NM). No Florida or PANYNJ launch has been announced by the FAA.

facts.fact: Selections span 26 states (March 2026 release and 2026-09-10 TX release). Later FAA releases (2026-09-23 NC, 2026-10-19 NM, 2026-10-21 BETA certificate) say 28 states. The FAA has never published a state list.
More than 30 proposals were received; projects were evaluated by a DOT/FAA technical review team.
Program director Tina Buelo (2026-06-09): no OTAs signed yet; signing starts a 90-day clock to begin operations.
FAA fact sheet: eIPP is not a mechanism to bypass certification. Aircraft must already be in FAA type certification. The program runs three years after the first project becomes operational.
2026-10-21: FAA issued BETA the first Special Airworthiness Market Survey Certificate for an eVTOL (ALIA A250). It expands the geographic scope of BETA's operations.

disagreements: State count: 26 (March 2026) vs 28 (FAA releases from 2026-09-23 on).

Launch order numbering: the 2026-09-10 TX release calls Texas the 'sixth location'. The 2026-09-23 NC release calls NC the 'fifth', following Texas. The 2026-10-19 NM release calls NM the 'sixth', following NC. Counting FAA flight releases gives PA, UT, LA, TX, NC, NM, so Texas is probably the fourth launch (the PA collaborative flew twice).

Start date: the March release said operations by summer 2026 (Morgan Lewis: June 2026). The first operation was 2026-07-10. Joby flew JFK to Manhattan demonstrations from 2026-04-27 under the PANYNJ banner, before any OTA was signed (Aerospace America, 2026-06-09), so the FAA does not count them as eIPP operations.

teams.summary: The Port Authority leads a bi-state NY/NJ project with Joby, Archer, BETA and Electra (the Port Authority also names Wisk). It covers 12 concepts, from Manhattan airport-to-heliport air taxis to upstate NY and Vermont cargo and medical flights based at Syracuse. The only flights so far are Joby's April 2026 demonstrations from JFK to three Manhattan heliports. The FAA has not announced a formal PANYNJ eIPP launch as of 2026-10-29.
disagreements: Partners: the FAA lists Archer, BETA, Electra and Joby; the Port Authority, via ROI-NJ, adds Wisk.
Geography: the FAA says 'across New England', but named sites are only in NY, NJ and (per BETA) VT. No CT, MA, RI, NH or ME site or agency was found.
The FAA says 'Manhattan heliport' (singular); the Joby demos used three heliports.

Joby calls the April campaign 'week-long', but a photo caption says 10-day. It came before any OTA (none signed as of 2026-06-09), and the FAA counts the 2026-07-10 PA flight as the first eIPP operation.
The Port Authority's own press page did not render, so its content comes from ROI-NJ and Transportation Today.

teams.summary: PennDOT leads the NASAO AAM Multistate Collaborative, which aims to revitalize regional air service like the Essential Air Service program. Its aircraft makers are BETA, Electra and Pivotal, its operators are United Therapeutics, UPMC STAT MedEvac, Nulton/Tri State Charter and Republic Airways, and it includes six universities. It flew the program's first operation, BETA's VA-to-MD organ delivery on 2026-07-10, and Electra's Manassas-to-Philadelphia hybrid-electric demos in August 2026.
disagreements: State count: the FAA says 13 states. The June 2026 Pivotal release lists 18, and BETA says 'Pennsylvania plus 17 other states'. Only PA, VA, MD and NJ have a confirmed operating role. The 18-state list overlaps other teams (NC, OK, OR, NM).
The FAA's 'Other' entry is not named. Pivotal and the four operators are inferred.
Electra aircraft: the FAA quotes the 'Ultra Short aircraft', while AIN says the EL2 demonstrator flew.
PennDOT's and NASAO's own release pages could not be read (403/Cloudflare), so the official state roster is unverified.

teams.summary: NCDOT's eLIFT-NC uses BETA's ALIA CX300 and Joby's autonomy-equipped J208 Caravan to test medical-logistics and disaster-response flights from the Research Triangle to eastern NC and the Outer Banks. ECU Health, WakeMed and UNC Health are health partners, and Metro Aviation flies the BETA aircraft. Flights began 2026-09-17, and the autonomous operation into Virginia has not flown yet.
disagreements: Pilot onboard: NCDOT's FAQ says every eLIFT-NC aircraft will carry a licensed pilot. The FAA calls the Joby J208 flight 'remotely piloted', and Joby calls it autonomous with a safety pilot.
The FAA's 'Other' entry is never named; Metro Aviation is the likely match.
Launch order: the FAA's NC release calls NC the 'fifth location', following Texas, but the Texas release called Texas the 'sixth'.
Unverified leads (search snippets only): NC State, NC A&T, Elizabeth City State University, Causey Aviation Unmanned, UPS Flight Forward.

teams.summary: Albuquerque's Aviation Department works with Reliable Robotics to fly a remotely piloted Cessna 208B Caravan for regional cargo, with planned routes to Santa Fe and Durango, Colorado. The first demonstration flights were two days at the Sunport in mid-October 2026, with a safety pilot aboard. The Santa Fe and Durango routes have not flown yet.
disagreements: Urban Air Mobility News calls the ABQ event 'hybrid-electric', but the Caravan is not hybrid. This is likely boilerplate carried over from other releases.
Start date: testing was expected in August 2026, but the first flights came in mid-October.
'Remotely piloted' (FAA) vs safety pilot aboard (Albuquerque Journal).
